Exercise: Single-Arm Push-Up

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- push

Primary Muscles:

- chest

Secondary Muscles:

- shoulders
- triceps

Equipment:

- bodyweight

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- hypertrophy
- strength

Contraindications:

- condition: shoulder injury, description: May exacerbate shoulder injuries due to increased load on the shoulder joint.
- condition: recent surgery, description: Avoid until full recovery, as it may strain healing tissues.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Single-Arm Push-Up with Alternating Arm, instructions: ['Perform the same movement but switch arms after each rep.']
- name: Single-Arm Push-Up with Pause at Bottom, instructions: ['Lower yourself by allowing the elbow to flex until you touch the ground, pause for 1-2 seconds, then reverse direction be extending the arm to return to the starting position.']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Push-Up, equipment: dumbbells

Instructions:

- Begin laying prone on the ground. Move yourself into a position supporting your weight on your toes and one arm. Your working arm should be placed directly under the shoulder, fully extended. Your legs should be extended, and for this movement you may need a wider base, placing your feet further apart than in a normal push-up.
- Maintain good posture, and place your free hand behind your back. This will be your starting position.
- Lower yourself by allowing the elbow to flex until you touch the ground.
- Descend slowly, and reverse direction be extending the arm to return to the starting position.
